api_consensus_validators_explorer_balanc.description:
Balance-distribution histogram across co-validators sharing a withdrawal credential.
Light view over fct_consensus_validators_status_latest (~558k rows); the API prunes
by withdrawal_credentials before the bucketing runs so the query is cheap even
without a physical index on credentials.

Bucket edges (<1, 1-16, 16-32, 32-48, 48-64, 64-128, 128-256, >=256 GNO) are chosen
to span the two MaxEB regimes: 0x00 / 0x01 credentials cap at 32 GNO effective
balance (pre-Pectra), while 0x02 compounders + EIP-7251 go up to 2048 GNO
post-Pectra. The 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 edges surface clusters at both caps plus
any partial-balance validators (withdrawing or slashed). bucket_order (0-7) is
emitted to keep the API sort stable in ascending balance order.

api_consensus_validators_search.description:
Dropdown source for the Validator Explorer tab. Grain is one row per
WITHDRAWAL_CREDENTIALS (not per validator) — on Gnosis today this is ~3,400 rows
vs 558k at validator-grain, so the dashboard can load the full list in a single
request (a few hundred KB on the wire) without 30s timeouts.

Collapsing to credential-grain matches the Explorer tab's semantics: every chart
on that tab aggregates across all validators sharing the selected
withdrawal_credentials. A solo validator is just a "credential with
validator_count = 1"; an operator is "credential with validator_count = N".

display_name is shaped as
    '<prefix-4>…<address-tail-10> · N validator(s) (v#<first-index>)'
using the tail of the credential (the actual execution address) so operators with
the same 0x01 type-byte prefix remain visually distinguishable.

LabelSelector filters client-side on substring match against every column the API
returns, so pasting a withdrawal_credentials string from a block explorer or wallet
finds the exact row. Pasting a validator_index or pubkey not in this column won't
match here — those lookups need /api/validators_performance_latest, which stays at
per-validator grain.
api_consensus_validators_search.name: api_consensus_validators_search

api_execution_circles_v2_avatar_trust_ne.description:
Trust-network edge list for the Circles v2 Avatar Trust Network panel.

One row per directed trust edge from the perspective of the focal
avatar. For mutual relationships TWO rows are emitted (avatar →
counterparty AND counterparty → avatar) so the chart renders both
arrows. The dashboard's avatar global filter scopes rows to one focal
avatar — ClickHouse pushes that filter down into each UNION branch, so
per-request cost stays small despite the apparent size of the query.
Materialising this globally would produce ~millions of rows × long IPFS
strings and blow the memory budget, so this stays a view on purpose.

Each row carries display name and IPFS preview image for both
endpoints (joined from api_execution_circles_v2_avatar_metadata). The
dashboard graph chart consumes these via sourceImageField /
targetImageField to render avatar thumbnails on the nodes. The
target_layer / source_layer columns drive the chart's concentric
layout: "Focal avatar" lives at the centre, "Mutual" forms the inner
ring, "Trust given" the middle ring, "Trust received" the outer ring.
api_execution_circles_v2_avatar_trust_ne.name: api_execution_circles_v2_avatar_trust_network

api_execution_gnosis_app_time_to_first_c.description:
Time from onboard to a user's FIRST event of each conversion kind, bucketed
by onboard-month cohort. Long format: one row per (cohort_month,
conversion_kind) over topup / swap_filled / marketplace_buy /
token_offer_claim. Built on int_execution_gnosis_app_first_conversion.

Modeling assumptions:
  * cohort_month = toStartOfMonth(first_seen_at), the heuristic onboard
    month. The current (partial) month is excluded.
  * n_in_cohort = all users onboarded that month; n_converted = those with a
    non-NULL first_<kind>_at (a NULL first_*_at means the user never did that
    action). pct_converted = n_converted / n_in_cohort x 100.
  * median/p25/p75_days are over CONVERTERS ONLY, as
    dateDiff('day', first_seen_at, first_conversion_at), FLOORED AT 0: the
    heuristic onboard date can postdate a user's real first action (negative
    raw diff), and those users are reported as 0-day rather than negative.

api_execution_lending_borrowers_count_7d.description:
KPI view of recently-active borrowers on Gnosis (Aave V3, SparkLend).
IMPORTANT — this is a 7-day FLOW, not a stock: unique wallets that emitted a
Borrow within the trailing 7 days (bitmap-merged from fct_execution_lending_latest,
granularity:last_7d). It is NOT symmetric with api_execution_lending_lenders_count_7d,
which is a point-in-time balance STOCK (wallets with a positive supply balance on
the latest date). Do not compare the two side by side as like-for-like — lenders =
balance stock, borrowers = 7-day borrow activity. (A true borrower STOCK would
require per-wallet debt balances, which user_balances_daily does not currently track.)
One row per protocol plus an 'ALL'-protocols aggregate. change_pct compares against
the equivalent 7-day count one week earlier.
api_execution_lending_borrowers_count_7d.name: api_execution_lending_borrowers_count_7d

api_execution_lending_lenders_count_7d.description:
KPI view of currently-active lenders on Gnosis (Aave V3, SparkLend).
"Active lenders" is a STOCK measure — unique wallets currently holding a
positive supply balance in a lending market on Gnosis (point-in-time count),
not a flow measure (users who supplied within a window).

One row per protocol plus an 'ALL'-protocols aggregate row (distinct
wallets across both markets). change_pct compares today's active count vs
the count from 7 days ago on the same balance snapshot (users whose
balance was positive then, regardless of whether they're still active now).

api_execution_live_trades.description: Dashboard-facing feed of recent DEX trades on Gnosis Chain. Reads from the cached `int_live__dex_trades_raw` table, so user queries never hit source logs or trigger decode-log scans. Last 30 minutes of CACHED data (anchored on `max(block_timestamp)` in that table, which trails the live source by the incremental refresh cadence) with a 60-second reorg buffer. Multi-hop router swaps are collapsed to one row per transaction. Dust is filtered via `live_trades_min_usd` var (default 1 USD); rows with unknown USD are kept. No LIMIT is applied — dashboards should add their own. For ingestion-level staleness, query `api_execution_live_trades_freshness` separately.
api_execution_live_trades.name: api_execution_live_trades

lag_seconds.description: Seconds between `newest_block_timestamp` and `server_now`. Higher = staler data.

api_execution_live_trades_freshness.description: One-row freshness indicator for the live-trades tab. Shows the newest ingested block timestamp in `execution_live.logs`, the server clock, and the lag in seconds. Intended for a "Data as of X, lag Y min" UI element — important because the tab is anchored on ingested-data time, not wall clock. Reads directly from the source so it keeps working when the feed itself is empty.

api_mixpanel_ga_growth_campaign_weekly.description:
GROWTH — campaign-attributable Gnosis App conversion funnel by UTM campaign x week.
Aggregate-only projection of api_mixpanel_ga_gnosis_app_acquisition_weekly with the
causal-validity treatment applied: first_touch only, clipped to week >= 2025-10-01
(Mixpanel era), and the touch-precedence gate (a campaign is credited only when its
touch preceded the conversion). conversion_kind in (topup, starts_referring,
swap_filled, token_offer_claim); topup is the attributable "funded" proxy. Only ~4-7%
of in-era app conversions carry a causally-valid campaign; the rest are
utm_campaign='unknown'. Served via the metrics-dashboard x-api-key layer
(blanket-excluded from cerebro-api).

contracts_UniswapV3_Pool_events_live.description: Plain view over `execution_live.logs` that decodes Uniswap V3 Pool events in near-real-time. Materialized as a view (not a materialized_view) because the cryo-live indexer populates logs via bulk part attaches that do not fire MV triggers. The source is pre-filtered to the last 4h (relative to the source HWM, not wall-clock) so the decode_logs scan stays fast instead of covering the full 48h TTL. The filter lands inside the macro's FROM clause — before the dedup window function and ABI join — which is the only position where ClickHouse can use it for partition/granule skipping.
contracts_UniswapV3_Pool_events_live.name: contracts_UniswapV3_Pool_events_live

contracts_gpay_modules_registry.description:
Cross-referenced registry of every Zodiac module proxy that is currently
or was ever enabled on a Gnosis Pay Safe.

Two evidence sources, joined on the proxy address:
  1. int_execution_safes_module_events — the Safe enabled this address
     as a module (filtered to GP Safes via int_execution_gpay_wallets).
  2. int_execution_zodiac_module_proxies — the address was deployed by
     the canonical Zodiac ModuleProxyFactory and points at one of the
     three known GP mastercopies.

The INNER JOIN means we drop any "enabled module" event that points to
an address we don't recognise as a Zodiac proxy of a GP-relevant type.
This is the high-quality registry that decode_logs consumes via
contract_address_ref to decode per-module events downstream.

Output schema matches the standard contracts_*_registry shape so
decode_logs picks up abi_source_address automatically.

contracts_safe_registry.description:
Registry consumed by decode_logs(contract_address_ref=ref('contracts_safe_registry')).
Maps each Safe proxy → the singleton whose ABI should be used to decode
its events.

Columns required by decode_logs:
  address              — the emitting contract (proxy)
  contract_type        — 'SafeProxy', so callers can pass contract_type_filter
  abi_source_address   — the singleton; decode_logs joins event_signatures
                         on (topic0, abi_source_address) to find the ABI
  is_dynamic           — 1 = discovered on-chain (all Safe proxies are)
  start_blocktime      — earliest block at which this proxy can emit events
  discovery_source     — provenance tag

Tiny model — one row per Safe (thousands to low millions). Materialized
as a table so decode_logs's compile-time get_columns_in_relation() works
the moment dbt runs the downstream events model.

crawlers_data.celo_gpay_transfers.description: Raw, UNCLASSIFIED whitelisted-token (USDT/USDC) ERC-20 transfers touching a Celo GP card Safe on either side. Deliberately not pre-classified here — Dune only does the extraction + wallet- membership + token-whitelist filtering that requires querying Celo chain data ClickHouse doesn't otherwise have; the actual Payment/Top-up/Withdrawal/Reversal classification happens in int_celo_gpay_activity.sql, mirroring how Gnosis Chain classifies from raw execution.logs rather than a pre-classified source. This keeps classification logic versioned/testable in dbt-cerebro instead of living in an external Dune query. Ingested by click-runner: a one-time full backfill since launch plus a daily 3-day-lookback incremental job (tolerates the job not running for up to 2 days straight), both writing into the same ReplacingMergeTree table. Deduped via `OPTIMIZE ... FINAL` after every insert (see queries/celo_gpay/optimize_celo_gpay_transfers.sql) so the overlap window never double-counts on same-day reads.
crawlers_data.celo_gpay_transfers.name: crawlers_data.celo_gpay_transfers

crawlers_data.celo_gpay_wallet_events.description: Unified, append-only wallet-lifecycle event log for Celo GP card Safes: issued_at (initial owner(s) at SafeSetup, one row per owner) + add_owner + remove_owner. Replaces the earlier separate celo_gpay_wallets (a per-safe snapshot table whose is_activated/first_spend_at/owner_address MUTATED in place on every daily refresh) and celo_gpay_owner_events tables — feedback from review was that any source where rows change value over time (not append-only) will break incremental models built on top of it, and this is not a hypothetical: an incremental model that already processed a row before a late-arriving fact caught up has no mechanism to revisit it. An append-only log has no row that can ever change, so it's immune to that failure class by construction rather than by careful, easy-to-forget engineering discipline (full-rebuild wallets + wide-enough incremental windows) elsewhere in the pipeline. first_spend_at/is_activated are deliberately NOT events here — derived in dbt directly from crawlers_data.celo_gpay_transfers instead (the fact is already fully present there — anything sent to the settlement address, the same definition the Dune spine itself uses for its own activation signal — so ingesting it separately would just store the same fact twice). Discovered while building this: GP's Celo provisioning flow commonly swaps a Safe's owner within seconds of SafeSetup —in the simplest observed case, the real EOA owner is removed and replaced with a hardcoded dead/sentinel address (0x...002), permanently disabling owner-based signing so only the Roles/Delay module can move funds; more complex multi-owner reconfigurations (1 remove + multiple adds) have also been observed, so this is real variation worth tracking as data, not a single deterministic rule to hardcode. int_celo_gpay_wallets.owner_address (identity) reads only the issued_at events and intentionally never reflects this later churn — mirrors Gnosis Chain's initial_owner vs current-owner split exactly (int_execution_gpay_user_identity_bridge vs int_execution_gpay_wallet_owners). Deliberately minimal columns — no tx_hash/log_index, since nothing downstream reads them; the current-owners fold's same-timestamp tie-break is resolved entirely in dbt (see int_celo_gpay_safe_current_owners.sql) without needing raw chain log metadata. Ingested by click-runner: a one-time full backfill since launch plus a daily 3-day-lookback incremental job (tolerates the job not running for up to 2 days straight), same shape as celo_gpay_transfers.
crawlers_data.celo_gpay_wallet_events.name: crawlers_data.celo_gpay_wallet_events

crawlers_data.gp_migrated_safes.description:
OLD -> NEW Safe mapping for the June 2026 post-exploit Gnosis Pay migration. One row per migrated Safe; a NEW Safe never appears as an OLD Safe, so a single hop resolves fully. Static dataset - the migration completed 2026-06-08 and no further rows are expected.
Holds GnosisPay customer Safe addresses and is therefore SENSITIVE: it was previously a repo seed and must NOT be returned to one. This repo is public; the mapping is not derivable from public chain state (old and new Safes share no user-level owner by design, since the migration issued new signers), so publishing it would be a genuine disclosure rather than a convenience. See cerebro-mcp/docs/compliance/gdpr-audit-2026-07.md section 7.
crawlers_data.gp_migrated_safes.name: crawlers_data.gp_migrated_safes

crawlers_data.gpay_operational_wallets.description:
Gnosis Pay company-operated wallet addresses (treasury, relayers, settlement). Used purely as an EXCLUSION list so company wallets are not counted as users. These belong to a legal person, not a natural person, so they are out of GDPR scope - do NOT pseudonymize them: both call sites join against plaintext on-chain addresses, so hashing would break the exclusion for no privacy gain.
Changes to this list silently move user counts. Treat edits as reviewable changes, not routine data updates.

fct_celo_gpay_balances_safe_daily.description:
DENSE per-Safe/token/day net-flow balance (Celo analog of Gnosis Chain's
int_execution_gpay_balances_user_daily). Densified over a date spine so
downstream daily totals and latest-day snapshots are correct on every day.
Net flow = (Top-up + Reversal) - (Payment + Withdrawal). Equals the true
on-chain balance ONLY for USDC/USDT under the documented scope assumptions
(see file header). Not a chain-wide balance snapshot.

fct_consensus_validators_apy_mean_daily.description:
Network-wide daily mean APY, balance-weighted by balance_prev_gno so exited / idle
/ just-entered validators (apy=0 and/or tiny balance) don't drag the average down
to meaninglessly low values. Output aligns with the median of the APY Distribution
chart, which effectively filters those validators via its quantile window.

    apy = SUMIf(apy * balance_prev_gno, 0 < apy < 200 AND balance_prev_gno > 0)
          / NULLIF(SUMIf(balance_prev_gno, 0 < apy < 200 AND balance_prev_gno > 0), 0)

Outlier filter (apy in (0, 200)) matches int_consensus_validators_dists_daily.
Zero-APY rows are dropped — they include exited validators that contributed nothing
but were once active, plus validators still in the entry queue.

Materialized as a physical table so the dashboard API returns in milliseconds:
running balance-weighted SUMIf over the 200M-row income fact would 30s-timeout
Vercel functions. Output is ~1568 rows, trivial to rebuild whenever the upstream
int_consensus_validators_income_daily updates.

fct_consensus_validators_explorer_daily.description:
Per-operator (withdrawal_credentials) daily roll-up feeding the five daily charts on
the Validator Explorer tab. Materialized as a physical table sorted on
withdrawal_credentials so the API's `WHERE withdrawal_credentials = 'x'` filter
prunes at read time via the primary index. Rebuilt incrementally month-by-month to
stay under the cluster's 10.8 GiB memory cap during backfill.

APY is balance-weighted (drops apy=0 idle validators):
    apy = SUMIf(apy * balance_prev_gno, 0 < apy < 200 AND balance_prev_gno > 0)
          / SUMIf(balance_prev_gno,        0 < apy < 200 AND balance_prev_gno > 0)
falling back to 0 when no validators qualify. See
api_consensus_validators_apy_mean_daily for the rationale.

v3: drops post-exit rows. Without this, an exited validator keeps emitting
zero-income / zero-balance rows from int_consensus_validators_income_daily forever,
which the UI renders as a flat tail on the credential's balance line. Joining
stg_consensus__time_helpers + status_latest and filtering
`date <= genesis + exit_epoch * slots_per_epoch * seconds_per_slot` (or exit_epoch
is FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH = 2^64-1, meaning "not exited") makes every chart downstream
stop at the validator's actual exit.

fct_consensus_validators_explorer_member.description:
Members table for the Validator Explorer tab: one row per validator under the
selected withdrawal credential. Reads int tables directly (cheap: ~558k status
rows + ~558k latest-day income rows) rather than routing through
api_consensus_validators_performance_latest.

v3 additions:
  * Lifecycle columns: activation_eligibility_epoch, activation_epoch, exit_epoch,
    withdrawable_epoch, slashed, plus derived activation_date / exit_date /
    withdrawable_date.
  * Per-validator balance-weighted 30-day APY:
        apy_30d = SUMIf(income, eff_balance > 0)
                  / NULLIF(AVGIf(eff_balance, eff_balance > 0), 0) * 365 * 100
    with zero-effective-balance rows excluded so idle slots don't pull the mean.
  * Driver is fct_consensus_validators_status_latest with LEFT JOIN into
    income/rewards so a validator still pending activation (no income rows) still
    appears as a row with status='pending_*' and zeros elsewhere — no silent
    row-drops on the join.

FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH sentinel (2^64 - 1 = 18446744073709551615) is emitted by the beacon
state for epochs that have not happened yet; these are NULLed out before converting
to dates so the UI renders a blank instead of a year in 292 billion AD. Otherwise,
derived dates are toDate(genesis_time_unix + epoch * slots_per_epoch * seconds_per_slot).

fct_execution_address_resolver.description:
Per-(address × source) domain resolver rows. The cross-source merge
happens at query time inside `api_execution_address_resolver` (point
lookup with `WHERE address = '0x…'` + `GROUP BY address`) instead of
at build time, because a 5–10M-address outer GROUP BY OOMs the cluster
cap. AggregatingMergeTree on `address` lets background merges collapse
duplicate rows when address is in only one source; the api view handles
the rest.

Materialised as a table (not a view) so the Account Portfolio custom
view's per-request lookup is an O(log N) primary-index seek rather
than a 5-way UNION scan. Expected cardinality ~500k-1M on Gnosis Chain.

display_name precedence: Circles avatar name → role tag ("Validator
operator · N validators" / "Safe owner · N safes" / "Safe contract" /
"Gnosis Pay wallet" / "Circles avatar") → empty. LabelSelector filters
on substring match so both hex paste and name search resolve from the
same field.
fct_execution_address_resolver.name: fct_execution_address_resolver

fct_execution_cow_trades.description: Canonical CoW Protocol trades table. Joins on-chain trade data from int_execution_cow_trades with off-chain protocol fee data from stg_crawlers_data__cow_api_trade_fees (ingested from the CoW API). fee_usd logic: pre-2024 CoW used an explicit fee model (fee_amount_raw > 0 in the Trade event); 2024+ CoW switched to surplus-based fees (not visible in events) sourced from executedProtocolFees via /api/v2/trades; the transition period (mid-2023 through early 2024) is mixed — COALESCE picks whichever source is available per trade. fee_source identifies where the fee came from ('onchain', 'api', or NULL). The API fee join is per fill — (order_uid, tx_hash, log_index) — because partially-fillable orders settle across multiple trades sharing an order_uid, each with its own executedProtocolFees; joining on order_uid alone double-counts fees across fills. NOTE — ClickHouse LEFT JOIN with join_use_nulls=0 (default) fills unmatched String columns with '' instead of NULL, so we check fee_token != '' rather than IS NOT NULL to correctly detect a real API match.

fct_execution_gnosis_app_attribution_30d.description:
Pre-computed first / last / linear / time-decay (half-life = 7d)
attribution per (`conversion_kind`, `event_kind`) over the last 180
days of conversions. The MTA persona reads this as the
attribution-comparison table; a single
`WHERE conversion_kind = '<kind>'` filter swaps in the desired
conversion target.

Implementation: pre-aggregate per conversion → tie-counts → per-touch
score → group by `event_kind`. Pure GROUP BY + LEFT JOIN; no
`groupArray + ARRAY JOIN` and no window functions. The pattern
survived three rewrites — v1 arrays and v2 windows both OOM'd at
the cluster's 10 GiB per-query cap on the 12 M-row journey set; v3
drops sort space from 12 M down to ~22 k per-conversion rows.

Time-decay weight per touch: `td_raw = exp(-lag_days / 7)`,
normalized so `Σ td_credit_per_conversion = 1.0`. First / last
credit splits across ties so `Σ first_touch_credit_per_conv = 1.0`
and `Σ last_touch_credit_per_conv = 1.0` exactly.
fct_execution_gnosis_app_attribution_30d.name: fct_execution_gnosis_app_attribution_30d

fct_execution_gnosis_app_funnel_daily.description:
Per-day funnel diagnostics over `int_execution_gnosis_app_user_events_unified`
using ClickHouse `windowFunnel`. Funnel definitions live in seed
`mta_funnels.csv` (funnel_name + step_1/2/3 event_kinds + window_seconds).

The model materialises one SELECT block per funnel via a Jinja loop
over `run_query(seed)` and UNION ALLs the results — required because
`windowFunnel(window_seconds)` needs `window_seconds` as a
compile-time literal (a CROSS JOIN against the seed with the column
is rejected by ClickHouse with BAD_ARGUMENTS at runtime).

Each output row is one (date, funnel_name, user) triple with `level`
= the max step reached by that user within `window_seconds` of their
first matching event. `level=0` rows are emitted for users who hit
step 1's event but not step 2 within the window.

Adding a funnel: append a row to `mta_funnels.csv`, run
`dbt seed --select mta_funnels`, then `dbt run` regenerates the model
automatically.

fct_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_topups_coh.description:
First-top-up cohort × subsequent-top-up retention.

Top-up definition is owned by int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_topups (a GP
"Crypto Deposit" into a currently-GA-owned wallet; see that model's docs).

Modeling assumptions:
  * cohort_month = month of the user's FIRST top-up (so the cohort is the
    first-top-up cohort, NOT the onboard cohort).
  * initial_users (denominator) = the month-0 cohort size. Here max(users)
    over activity months equals the month-0 count by construction (every
    member tops up in their first-top-up month and later months are subsets),
    so the max()-anchor is correct for this model — unlike the onboard-cohort
    retention marts, which require the explicit onboard-cohort denominator.
  * retention_pct = % of the first-top-up cohort still topping up in month N.

fct_execution_gnosis_app_journeys_30d.description:
Pre-joined GA-side journey spine with a 30-day lookback. One row per
(user_pseudonym, conversion_kind, conversion_ts, conversion_date,
event_kind) group — one row per conversion × distinct prior-30d touchpoint
event_kind (n_touches / first_touch_ts / last_touch_ts / td_sum measures),
NOT one row per touch; the conversion's own event kind is excluded. Built via
`build_journey_lookback(30, 'gnosis_app')` so the leakage guards
(`event_ts < conversion_ts` and
`event_kind != conversion_kind_to_event_kind(conversion_kind)`) are
applied at materialisation, not at query time.

The MTA persona reads this directly to score first/last/linear/
time-decay credit per touch without re-running the conversions ×
events self-join. The 7d / 14d / 60d sensitivity-sweep variants
(deferred) reuse the same macro with a different `lookback_days`
argument.

Incremental, monthly partition on `conversion_date`. Uses
`grace_hash` join algorithm to keep memory bounded across the
explicit lookback window.

fct_execution_gnosis_app_retention_by_ac.description:
Cohort retention split by activity_kind (swap_filled / swap_signed / topup /
marketplace_buy / token_offer_claim / circles_*). Same onboard-cohort anchor
and denominator as fct_execution_gnosis_app_retention_monthly.

Modeling assumptions:
  * cohort_month = the user's GLOBAL onboard month (first 'onboard' row) —
    the SAME anchor for every action, so denominators are comparable across
    action types.
  * users (numerator) = distinct cohort users who did THIS activity_kind in
    activity_month (lower triangle only, activity_month >= cohort_month).
  * initial_users (denominator) = onboard-cohort size = distinct users
    onboarded in cohort_month. NOT max(users) over months (peak-normalisation
    -> retention > 100%) and NOT the month-0 action adopters: because the
    numerator counts any cohort user doing the action each month (not a fixed
    followed sub-cohort), a later month can have more adopters than month 0,
    so only the full onboard cohort bounds the ratio at <= 100%.
  * retention_pct reads as "% of the onboard cohort doing this action in
    month N" (action adoption), not conditional stickiness. Small/rare
    actions therefore show low (correct) percentages, not ~100%.
fct_execution_gnosis_app_retention_by_ac.name: fct_execution_gnosis_app_retention_by_action_monthly

fct_execution_gnosis_app_retention_month.description:
Cohort retention grid for the Gnosis App onboard cohort.

Modeling assumptions:
  * cohort_month = month of the user's 'onboard' row (first-ever heuristic
    hit), NOT their first transactional activity.
  * activity_month = month of any subsequent non-onboard activity. Only the
    lower triangle is kept (activity_month >= cohort_month) so on-chain
    history predating the GA onboard does not create spurious cells.
  * initial_users (the retention denominator) = the onboard-cohort size,
    i.e. distinct users whose onboard month is cohort_month. It is
    deliberately NOT max(users) over activity months (peak-normalisation,
    which let retention exceed 100%) and NOT the month-0 actives: the
    numerator counts ANY cohort user active in activity_month (not a fixed
    followed sub-cohort), so only the full onboard cohort bounds it <= 100%.
  * retention_pct therefore reads as "% of the onboard cohort active in
    month N" (return/adoption), not the conditional stickiness of a followed
    sub-cohort.
  * amount_retention_pct anchors on the cohort's earliest activity-month
    amount (argMin over activity_month).
fct_execution_gnosis_app_retention_month.name: fct_execution_gnosis_app_retention_monthly

One row per Gnosis App on-chain user_pseudonym, with boolean flags
indicating which identification heuristic(s) fired and a high-
confidence flag (n_distinct_heuristics >= 2).

user_pseudonym is the canonical cross-domain join key
(sipHash64 of lowercased address with the project PII salt).
Same hash space as: fct_revenue_per_user_*,
fct_execution_gpay_users_distinct, and stg_mixpanel_ga__events.user_id_hash.
Powers cross-sector overlap queries through the semantic layer.

"Gnosis App" spans two complementary data domains: web/mobile
analytics (Mixpanel-sourced, models/mixpanel_ga/) and on-chain
behaviour (this module). Discovery queries for "Gnosis App users"
should surface metrics from both — synonyms on the semantic_model
are set up accordingly.

fct_execution_gpay_attribution_30d.description:
Pre-computed first / last / linear / time-decay (HL=7d) attribution
per (`conversion_kind`, `identity_role`, `event_kind`) over the last
180 days of conversions. Same shape as the GA attribution mart with
the role dimension added, so a single
`WHERE conversion_kind = 'gpay_payment' AND identity_role = 'initial_owner'`
filter pulls owner-grain attribution for payments without changing
SQL shape.

Implementation: pre-aggregate per conversion → tie counts →
per-touch score → group by `event_kind`. Same memory-safe
GROUP BY + LEFT JOIN pattern as the GA mart (see GA model header
for the v1 / v2 / v3 history).

Time-decay weight per touch: `td_raw = exp(-lag_days / 7)`,
normalized so `Σ td_credit_per_conversion = 1.0`. First / last
credit splits across ties.
fct_execution_gpay_attribution_30d.name: fct_execution_gpay_attribution_30d

fct_execution_gpay_journeys_30d.description:
Pre-joined GP-side journey spine with a 30-day lookback. One row per
(user_pseudonym, identity_role, conversion_kind, conversion_ts,
conversion_date, event_kind) group — one row per conversion × distinct
prior-30d touchpoint event_kind (n_touches / first_touch_ts / last_touch_ts
/ td_sum measures), NOT one row per touch. Built via
`build_journey_lookback(30, 'gpay')` — the same macro that powers
the GA spine, with `identity_role` matched on both sides of the
conversion ↔ events join so role-grain semantics are preserved
(treasury-grain conversions match treasury-grain touchpoints, etc.).

Leakage guards enforced at materialisation:
  * `e.event_ts < c.conversion_ts`
  * `e.identity_role = c.identity_role`
  * `e.event_kind != conversion_kind_to_event_kind(c.conversion_kind)`

Microbatched in 1-month chunks via `scripts/full_refresh/refresh.py`
(`meta.full_refresh.batch_months: 1`). A single 2-year full-refresh
OOM'd at the 10 GiB per-query cap because of the 3-role fan-out ×
all GP activity × 30-day lookback. Per-month batches fit
comfortably; the refresh script auto-retries the rare batch that
pushes the limit.
fct_execution_gpay_journeys_30d.name: fct_execution_gpay_journeys_30d

sweep variant of the canonical `_30d` mart. Built via
`build_journey_lookback(60, 'gpay')`. `identity_role` is matched
on both sides of the conversion ↔ events join so role-grain

  * `e.identity_role = c.identity_role`
  * `e.event_kind != conversion_kind_to_event_kind(c.conversion_kind)`

(`meta.full_refresh.batch_months: 1`). At 3-role × 60-day lookback ×
2-year history this is the heaviest of the journey marts —
individual monthly batches can transiently push the 10 GiB cluster
cap; the refresh script auto-retries the rare batch that does.

fct_execution_mmm_baseline_latest.description:
Per-(KPI, media) baseline KPI: the median KPI value during weeks
where the media's adstocked spend sits in the bottom decile. This
is the level the KPI sits at when the media is effectively zero —
used by `mmm_analyst` as the `baseline_kpi` input that anchors the
log-log response curve fit and the contribution-decomposition
intercept.

Adstock is computed inline as a geometric 8-week running window
with λ=0.5 (recent-week weight 1, prior-week 0.5, two-back 0.25,
…) per media column. The bottom-decile threshold is
`quantile(0.1)(adstock_v)` per (KPI, media) pair. The persona can
recompute with a different λ if a fit prefers it; this mart is a
canonical starting point.

Pairs with fewer than 5 low-spend weeks are dropped (HAVING clause)
because the median wouldn't be statistically meaningful — the
`n_low_spend_weeks > 5` test guards against schema drift bringing
them back.
fct_execution_mmm_baseline_latest.name: fct_execution_mmm_baseline_latest

(`abs(pearson_corr) > 0.9`) directly to identify pairs that need

unique pairs are emitted (`a.col_name < b.col_name`).

fct_execution_mmm_spine_weekly.description:
MMM weekly spine — wide pivot of `int_execution_mmm_kpis_weekly`,
`int_execution_mmm_media_weekly`, and `int_execution_mmm_controls_weekly`.
One row per `week`, one column per (kpi | media | control) name,
populated by `sumIf` against the long-form intermediates. Continuous
time — every week within the spine range exists, even when no
KPI / media / control rows reference it.

This is the single mart the MMM analyst's runtime mapping points at.
The persona reads it directly and runs adstock decay, Hill / log-log
response-curve fits, and contribution decomposition against the
`media_*` columns conditioned on `kpi_*` and `ctrl_*`.

Adding a new column: update the corresponding intermediate's UNION,
update the registry seed, then add a `sumIf` clause here for the
new name. Schema is wide-by-design and bounded by the registry
seeds (~30 cols today).

fct_execution_pools_il_daily.description: Pool-level Loss Versus Rebalancing (LVR) from actual swap flows. LVR measures the cost LPs pay to arbitrageurs — the value extracted via swap rebalancing. Sign convention: negative = loss (arbitrage extracted value), positive = gain. Swap events already embed the concentrated-liquidity math executed by the pool contract, so this captures V3 amplification without per-position tracking. Each day's swap flows are valued at that day's token prices, then summed over the 7-day window. lvr_apr_7d = (swap_flow_usd_7d − fees_usd_7d) / avg_tvl_7d × (365/7) × 100. Fees are subtracted because swap event amounts include fees on the input side.

fct_execution_safe_owner_pseudonyms.description:
Chain-wide Safe → owner pseudonym bridge. One row per current
(safe_address, owner) pair, hashed into the project-wide
`user_pseudonym` space via the `pseudonymize_address` macro.

Exists so that any sector mart whose `user_pseudonym` is the hash
of a Safe contract address (gpay pay_wallets, validator withdrawal
Safes, gnosis_app AA wallets, Circles avatar Safes, ...) can be
composed with any owner-keyed sector via two equi-joins:

    sector_A.user_pseudonym = bridge.safe_user_pseudonym
    bridge.owner_user_pseudonym = sector_B.user_pseudonym

Surfaced in the semantic layer (`semantic/authoring/execution/safe/
semantic_models.yml`) and bridged into every existing user-keyed
mart via `semantic/relationships/user_pseudonym.yml`. Grain is
`(safe_user_pseudonym, owner_user_pseudonym)`.

## Coverage caveat — read before sizing this against another mart

`safe_user_pseudonym` is ONLY the Safe-contract side of the bridge
by construction; EOA owners appear ONLY on the `owner_user_pseudonym`
side. So an outer-join cardinality like "how many of mart X's
pseudonyms appear as safe_user_pseudonym in the bridge" is NOT a
coverage metric — it's the fraction of X's pseudonyms that happen
to be Safe addresses.

Example: `fct_execution_gpay_users_distinct` (64,418 rows) is a
UNION of safe_self pseudonyms (32,209), initial_owner pseudonyms
(32,208) and the GP delegate (1). All 32,209 GP Safes are covered
here as `safe_user_pseudonym`. The remaining ~32k initial-owner
pseudonyms are EOAs by definition; they land on the
`owner_user_pseudonym` side. The relationship definitions in
`semantic/relationships/user_pseudonym.yml` declare BOTH directions
per mart so the planner can reach either pseudonym flavour.

fct_mixpanel_ga_gpay_crossdomain_daily.description:
Daily rollup of Gnosis Pay ↔ Mixpanel matching with role-bucket and
activity dimensions.

Privacy boundary: every cross-domain join uses the keyed pseudonym
from the pseudonymize_address macro, applied identically on both
sides. Raw EOAs and Safe addresses never appear in this output.

Methodology: a per-user identity bridge (matched_pairs) reads the
precomputed (user_id_hash, gp_safe, matched_roles) tuples directly
from fct_mixpanel_ga_gpay_users so the JOIN is not recomputed here.
Same gp_safe → activity flags (delay_active_safes_7d,
allowance_changed_safes_30d) are computed once and joined into both
rollups. mp_user_flags rolls up role flags and activity flags to one
row per Mixpanel user; mp_daily then computes per-day matched-user
counts sliced by role bucket and activity flag, and gpay_daily
contributes the on-chain DAU comparison.

Implementation note: explicit AS aliases on the mp.* columns in the
final SELECT are required. Both mp_daily and gpay_daily expose a
`date` column, so ClickHouse keeps the qualified name `mp.date` in
the output projection and the config's order_by=(date) would
otherwise fail to resolve. The non-ambiguous columns get explicit
aliases too as a defensive consistency pass.

Headline metrics:
  mp_dau                — Mixpanel daily active users (production,
                          all identification states; anonymous
                          device users are counted but never match
                          the GP side).
  onchain_active_users  — distinct GP wallets with on-chain
                          activity that day, from
                          fct_execution_gpay_activity_daily.
  matched_users_any     — DAU users matched on ANY identity role
                          (initial_owner ∪ delegate ∪ safe_self).
  matched_by_*          — same DAU users sliced by which role
                          matched.
  users_with_delay_activity_7d
                        — matched users whose gp_safe queued at
                          least one TransactionAdded event in the
                          last 7 days.
  users_with_allowance_changes_30d
                        — matched users whose gp_safe had a
                          SetAllowance event in the last 30 days.

Backwards-compat: the original `matched_users` and `match_rate_pct`
columns are preserved (now equal to matched_users_any and the
corresponding rate) so existing dashboards keep working.
fct_mixpanel_ga_gpay_crossdomain_daily.name: fct_mixpanel_ga_gpay_crossdomain_daily

fct_mixpanel_ga_gpay_users.description:
Per-user fact joining Mixpanel identified users to Gnosis Pay Safes
through the keyed-pseudonym identity bridge.

One row per (user_id_hash, gp_safe) pair where the user matched on
at least one of the three identity roles (initial_owner, delegate,
safe_self). Denormalizes the per-Safe module topology, current daily
limit, and recent delay activity onto each row so downstream segment
queries don't need extra joins.

Privacy invariant: every column representing a person is either
user_id_hash (already pseudonymized in stg_mixpanel_ga__events) or a
Safe address (smart account, treated as non-PII). No raw EOA appears.

Implementation note: explicit AS aliases on the m.* columns in the
final SELECT are required. ClickHouse keeps the qualified name
`m.gp_safe` in the output projection whenever the bare name `gp_safe`
is ambiguous across joined relations (modules_per_safe,
allowance_per_safe, delay_30d, spends_30d all expose a `gp_safe`
column), and the config's order_by=(user_id_hash, gp_safe) would
then fail to resolve.

HEADLINE — cross-stream unique-active-user cohort (rolling 52-week).
For each user, fees across ALL streams (holdings + sDAI + GPay) and

$-cohort. Because aggregation happens before bucketing, a user
cannot appear in multiple cohorts even if they accrue fees in
several sectors. This is the canonical cross-sector "active user"
breakdown by economic size; the `$1+`/`$6+`/... buckets are

int_celo_gpay_activity.description:
Per-transfer classified Celo GP activity. Classification happens HERE,
not upstream in Dune — Dune only supplies raw whitelisted-token transfers
touching a GP Safe (crawlers_data.celo_gpay_transfers: sender, receiver,
token, amount). This mirrors int_execution_gpay_activity on Gnosis Chain,
which also classifies from raw log data rather than a pre-classified
source, so fixing/extending classification is a dbt edit + re-run here,
not a Dune query edit + re-backfill.
Actions: Payment (Safe -> AggregateBridge settlement), Withdrawal (Safe
-> anything else, including hypothetically another GP Safe), Reversal
(AggregateBridge -> Safe; a processor-side refund of a failed/disputed
charge), Top-up (anything else -> Safe, e.g. a MiniPay funding wallet).
No Cashback action exists; the GNO cashback program is Gnosis Chain only.
CASE ordering in the model checks sender-based branches (Payment/
Withdrawal) before receiver-based branches (Reversal/Top-up) — required
so a hypothetical Safe-to-Safe transfer classifies as a Withdrawal from
the sending Safe, not a Top-up to the receiving Safe (safe_address always
resolves to sender when sender is a Safe, so action must agree).
Rows where neither sender nor receiver matches int_celo_gpay_wallets are
dropped, not guessed at — observed in practice (2026-07-02 test backfill,
3 rows) as a real race between crawlers_data.celo_gpay_transfers and
int_celo_gpay_wallets, which are each independently derived from the same
live, continuously-indexing Dune spine rather than one consistent
snapshot: a brand-new Safe's transfer can be extracted moments before
that same Safe lands in the wallets snapshot.
materialized='incremental' with incremental_strategy='insert_overwrite'
and apply_monthly_incremental_filter (same macro/pattern already used by
Gnosis Chain's int_execution_gpay_activity_daily and
int_execution_gpay_wallet_owners) — recomputes the whole current
calendar-month partition every run, not just literally-new rows. This is
what preserves the self-healing behavior above under incremental
materialization: a Safe recognized a few seconds/minutes late (the only
lag actually observed) gets correctly reclassified on the next run as
long as it's within the same month. int_celo_gpay_wallets itself stays a
full rebuild regardless (see that model's own doc) — only this
per-transfer model needs incrementality, since it's the one whose row
count scales with transaction volume, not signup volume.
int_celo_gpay_activity.name: int_celo_gpay_activity

earliest submitted request_slot. is_self_consolidation is derived from
(source_pubkey == target_pubkey). The dedup matters because the raw
consensus.execution_requests.payload.consolidations array records every
operator resubmission, while the beacon chain only processes the first
valid request per source (and rejects later resubmissions). On heavy
consolidation days this inflated downstream target_inflow_gno by up to
8× before the fix landed. A validator may legitimately have BOTH a
self-consolidation (credential switch 0x01 → 0x02) and a later
cross-consolidation (balance transfer out, validator exits), which is
why dedup partitions by (source, is_self) rather than by source alone.

int_consensus_validators_consolidations_.description:
EIP-7251 (MaxEB) consolidation events at per-(date, validator_index, role) grain. See
https://notes.ethereum.org/@fradamt/maxeb-consolidation for the spec. Materialized as a
table because consolidations are rare and the application day can lag the request by
weeks, breaking monthly-partitioned incremental assumptions.

Two flavours emitted:
  * Self-consolidation (source_pubkey == target_pubkey): a credential switch
    0x01 -> 0x02 with no balance transfer. Emitted on the request day with
    role='self', transferred_amount_gno = 0.
  * Cross-consolidation (source != target): processed at the source's withdrawable
    epoch — the source's full effective balance transfers to the target and the
    source exits. Emitted on the inferred APPLICATION day for both source
    (role='source') and target (role='target'); if application has not yet occurred
    no row is emitted (a later run will pick it up).

Application day is inferred as the first day at/after the request where the source
validator's effective_balance_gwei first reaches 0. transferred_amount_gno is taken
as the source's last non-zero effective balance, observed regardless of whether that
day is before or after the request day — Gnosis's high churn limit means a
consolidation can apply in the same slot as the request, leaving no post-request
eb>0 row to capture.

Pubkey -> validator_index resolution reads fct_consensus_validators_status_latest
(not int_consensus_validators_labels) so exited source validators — by definition
every successful consolidation source — remain resolvable. JOINs are pre-filtered
to only the pubkeys appearing in the current batch's requests, and the source
snapshot lookup is bounded to a tight window (-7d/+30d around request_date) so
the build doesn't OOM on busy months.

v4 (2026-04): final aggregation grain matches the ReplacingMergeTree unique_key
(date, validator_index, role). When N sources consolidate into the same target
on the same application day the per-counterparty fidelity is collapsed — the
target row carries transferred_amount_gno = SUM(incoming), cnt = N, and
counterparty_validator_index = any() representative. Before this fix, emitting
one row per (date, validator_index, role, counterparty) made all but one of the
N target rows get silently dropped by ReplacingMergeTree dedup, under-crediting
the target by (N-1)*32 GNO and corrupting per-validator income in
int_consensus_validators_income_daily. Mass-balance invariant
SUMIf(transferred_amount_gno, role='source') = SUMIf(transferred_amount_gno, role='target')
per date is enforced by tests/consensus_consolidations_mass_balance.sql.

v5 (2026-04): transferred_amount_gno is the source's last-observed REAL balance
(balance_gwei / 1e9 / 32, in real GNO), not its effective balance. Effective balance is a stepped
function that over-reports the actual mass moved when a source has accrued inactivity
penalties; using real balance makes the target's consolidation_inflow_gno match the
target's actual balance delta, eliminating the ~10-120 GNO per-target "loss" days
seen under v4 on heavy-consolidation events. After this change, the target's
consensus_income_amount_gno on the application day is ~0 (pure reward) rather than
slightly negative. The sweep still uses effective_balance_gwei=0 as the
application-day indicator.
int_consensus_validators_consolidations_.name: int_consensus_validators_consolidations_daily

÷ √(network_effective_balance_gwei) ÷ 1e9 ÷ 32. Anything above this in daily balance
growth is attributed to effective_deposits_credited_gno, not income. Useful for
debugging and for constructing validator-balance-weighted APY.

int_consensus_validators_income_daily.description:
Daily per-(date, validator_index) consensus income fact, including exited and
zero-balance validators. Amount columns in GNO. Identifier columns (pubkey,
withdrawal_credentials, withdrawal_address, status) are joined at the API layer from
int_consensus_validators_snapshots_daily to keep this table memory-efficient.

Two deposit numbers are emitted because of the post-Pectra accounting problem:
pre-Pectra, beacon-chain deposits credited the same day they were requested. Post
EIP-7002 / EIP-7251 (MaxEB) a single execution-request can ask for up to 2048 GNO
for one validator, but the beacon chain credits it gradually through the
pending_deposits queue (churn-bounded), so a 1767-GNO request can land as ~0.01 GNO
on the request day and ~1 GNO/day for weeks afterward. The naive
income = balance_delta - reported_deposit + withdrawals - cons_net then produces
catastrophic per-day errors (~-1767 GNO on request day, large false positives on
drain days).

Fix: spec-bounded effective-credit. The consensus spec gives a closed-form maximum
reward per epoch per validator,
    base_reward_per_epoch = effective_balance_gwei * BASE_REWARD_FACTOR
                          / sqrt(total_active_effective_balance_gwei)
With Gnosis constants BASE_REWARD_FACTOR=25, SLOTS_PER_EPOCH=16, SECONDS_PER_SLOT=5
(so EPOCHS_PER_DAY = 86400 / (5*16) = 1080) and a 3x safety multiplier for
attestation + proposer + sync duties, we get
    expected_reward_cap = 3 * effective_balance_gwei * 25 * 1080
                        / sqrt(network_active_effective_balance_gwei)        (in gwei)
    effective_deposits_credited = GREATEST(
        0,
        balance_delta + withdrawals - cons_net - expected_reward_cap
    )
    consensus_income_amount_gno = balance_delta
                                - effective_deposits_credited
                                + withdrawals - cons_net
This caps daily income at the spec maximum, keeps cumulative balance-flow exact,
leaves queued-but-not-yet-credited deposits in reported_deposit until the balance
actually moves, and scales with both validator size and total network stake.
Same base_reward * sqrt(total_stake)^-1 relation used by beaconcha.in's calculator,
applied here as a validity bound on observed income rather than a forward projection.

NOT additionally capped at reported_deposit: post-Pectra, on a queue-drain day the
reported amount is 0 but the balance jumps by hundreds of GNO; capping at reported
would falsely attribute the jump to income. The spec cap alone is sufficient.
Edge cases handled: pure reward day, reported-but-not-credited, queue-drain, slashing,
and consolidation source/target all reconcile correctly.

Cumulatives use effective credits (cumulative_deposits_gno) for total_income_estimated_gno;
cumulative_reported_deposits_gno is kept alongside for audit. Incremental strategy
follows int_execution_tokens_balances_native_daily — daily deltas + balance reads
are pulled only from the incremental window, with prior-state (last balance and
cumulatives at the previous partition boundary) loaded from  so lifetime
cumulatives stay correct without scanning history. balance_prev_gno uses lagInFrame
within the window, falling back to prev_state at the partition boundary.

Known upstream limitation: consensus.validators crawler outages (observed
2025-12-10 .. 2025-12-28, 20 fully-empty days) cause withdrawals/deposits/
consolidations during the gap to have no matching snapshot, producing a large
one-day negative income on the resume day for affected validators. Documented
here so consumers know those single-day outliers are upstream-data, not formula.

int_execution_address_roles_current.description:
Identity-role pivot: one row per on-chain address with boolean flags
for every role it plays across the sectors we track (Safe, GPay,
Circles, DeFi pools/lending, validator withdrawal, Dune labels).
Powers the Graph Explorer's node-kind badges and auto-discovery of
applicable graph profiles when a user seeds from a bare address.

Implementation: each per-source CTE first aggregates to ONE ROW PER
UNIQUE ADDRESS with its flag and any metadata already collapsed via
any() / max(). This compresses huge upstreams (dex_liquidity_events
at billions of rows, transfers at hundreds of millions) down to
millions of unique addresses BEFORE the UNION ALL. A single final
GROUP BY address then coalesces flags across sources. Memory stays
bounded by |unique addresses| x |source blocks|, not by upstream row
counts. The DEX scan emits both lp-provider and pool rows in one pass
via arrayJoin to halve memory + IO.

int_execution_circles_v2_avatar_metadata.description:
SCD-style historical view of every Circles v2 avatar metadata change.
One row per (avatar, metadata_digest) ever announced by the NameRegistry,
in event order, with valid_from / valid_to / is_current columns so the
dashboard can render the full timeline of name + image changes per avatar.
valid_to is computed via leadInFrame over (avatar) ordered by
(block_timestamp, log_index) and is NULL on the most recent row per
avatar. The parsed JSON fields (name, symbol, description, imageUrl,
previewImageUrl) are joined per (avatar, metadata_digest) from the most
recent successful fetch in circles_avatar_metadata_raw.

Incremental strategy: delete+insert keyed on (avatar, metadata_digest).
The affected_avatars CTE uses the standard apply_monthly_incremental_filter
macro (same as other Circles intermediates) to find any avatar that
received an UpdateMetadataDigest event in the incremental window, then
INNER JOINs the targets view to that set so the full history of every
affected avatar is recomputed in one shot — guaranteeing the leadInFrame
window function still sees every event for those avatars and valid_to
stays correct.

int_execution_circles_v2_mint_events.description:
One row per protocol mint, tagged with `mint_kind`. Sourced from the DECODED Hub events in contracts_circles_v2_Hub_events — NOT inferred from from=0x00…00 TransferSingle legs.
Classifier:
  personal  - PersonalMint event. to_address / token_address = the minting
              human; amount_raw = event `amount`. Replaces the old
              from=0x0 + Human-token heuristic, which over-counted ~4.5k
              avatars whose CRC was created only by inline auto-issuance
              legs that emit no PersonalMint event. Now matches Dune
              query_6317871 / hub_evt_personalmint (~18.4k distinct humans).
  group     - GroupMint event. to_address = receiver, token_address =
              group, operator = sender, amount_raw = Σ event `amounts[]`.
  migration - V1→V2 migration mints have no Hub mint event, so this branch
              stays transfer-derived: from=0x0 TransferSingle whose operator
              is the Circles V2 Migration contract
              (contracts_circles_registry.contract_type = 'Migration').

Incremental, monthly partitioned on block_timestamp.

int_execution_gnosis_app_bundlers.description:
Dynamic Cometh ERC-4337 bundler allowlist for Gnosis App attribution.
Supersedes the hand-maintained seeds/gnosis_app_relayers.csv, which listed
only 3 of ~61 real bundlers (so ~10% of GA users were missed; miss-rate hit
16-22% for Mar-2026+ cohorts when the 0x4337... fleet launched).

A bundler qualifies if it sends UserOps to the EntryPoint and either
(a) matches the Cometh vanity prefix 0x4337..., or (b) relayed a
GA-specific, relayer-agnostic anchor: a CRC fee transfer (ERC-1155 Hub or
gCRC ERC-20) to the fee receiver, or a GA InvitationModule RegisterHuman.
The curated seed is unioned in (belt-and-suspenders). Self-maintains as the
fleet rotates. Schema mirrors gnosis_app_relayers so consumers swap only the
ref().

int_execution_gnosis_app_conversions.description:
GA conversion registry — one row per observed conversion event,
with `conversion_kind` carried as a column rather than a separate
table per kind. The MTA persona filters with
`WHERE conversion_kind = '<kind>'` to swap conversion targets
without changing SQL shape.

Sources (UNION ALL):
  topup              ← int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_topups
  swap_filled        ← int_execution_gnosis_app_swaps WHERE was_filled
  token_offer_claim  ← int_execution_gnosis_app_token_offer_claims
  marketplace_buy    ← int_execution_gnosis_app_marketplace_payments

Each source INNER JOINs the identity bridge on lower(raw address) →
`user_pseudonym`, so this model never holds a raw address.

Incremental on `conversion_date` (monthly partition). The dedup key
`conversion_dedup_key` is a cityHash64 of the kind + the smallest
natural unique key per source (transaction_hash + log_index for
most; order_uid for swaps).

int_execution_gnosis_app_coverage_daily.description:
Per-day, per-conversion-kind tracked-coverage stats. The MTA
persona reads this to print the coverage block ("X% of topups on
date D had ≥1 touchpoint in the prior 30 days") without re-running
the conversion × events self-join.

"Tracked" definition: a conversion has at least one row in
`int_execution_gnosis_app_user_events_unified` whose `event_ts`
falls in `[conversion_ts - 30d, conversion_ts)` AND whose
`event_kind` is not the conversion's own mapped event_kind
(leakage guard via the `conversion_kind_to_event_kind` macro — a
`topup` conversion can't be tracked by its own `chain.topup` event).

Incremental, partitioned by month on `conversion_date`. Uses
`grace_hash` join algorithm in pre-hook because the events scan can
span the full 30-day lookback per conversion-month batch.

int_execution_gnosis_app_events_chain_un.description:
Long-form on-chain GA event log at full timestamp grain, keyed by
`user_pseudonym` (no raw address ever leaves the bridge). Single
source of chain-side touchpoints for MTA.

UNION ALL of seven CTEs, each tagged with a distinct `event_kind`
starting with `chain.`:

  chain.onboard               — first-ever heuristic hit per user
                                (from int_execution_gnosis_app_users_current)
  chain.<heuristic_kind>      — seven heuristic rules from
                                int_execution_gnosis_app_user_events
                                (circles_register_human, circles_invite_human,
                                circles_trust, circles_profile_update,
                                circles_fee, circles_personal_mint,
                                safe_invitation_module)
  chain.swap_signed           — every PreSignature event in
                                int_execution_gnosis_app_swaps
  chain.swap_filled           — was_filled subset, ts = first_fill_at
  chain.topup                 — int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_topups
  chain.marketplace_buy       — int_execution_gnosis_app_marketplace_payments
  chain.token_offer_claim     — int_execution_gnosis_app_token_offer_claims

int_execution_gnosis_app_first_conversio.description:
One row per Gnosis App user (the onboard cohort) with the date of their
first event in each conversion kind. Feeds the time-to-first-conversion view.

Modeling assumptions:
  * first_seen_at = the heuristic onboard date, carried from
    int_execution_gnosis_app_user_activity_daily ('onboard' rows).
  * Each first_<kind>_at is NULL when the user never did that action.
    This is enforced via nullIf(minIf(...), toDate('1970-01-01')) plus a
    join_use_nulls hook, so the ClickHouse Date default (1970-01-01) from an
    empty minIf or an unmatched LEFT JOIN cannot masquerade as a real
    conversion. Consumers MUST treat 1970-01-01 as impossible and rely on
    IS NULL (a prior bug let the epoch sentinel inflate pct_converted to
    100% and produce negative time-to-conversion).

int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_topups.description:
Gnosis App → Gnosis Pay top-ups.

A top-up = a Gnosis Pay "Crypto Deposit" into a GP wallet that is currently
GA-owned, per the persistent int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_wallets bridge
(is_currently_ga_owned), from the GA launch (2025-11-12) on. ga_user is the
wallet's first GA owner.

This supersedes the original same-transaction CoW-trade + deposit rule,
which captured only ~1.4% of GA-owned funding — most top-ups are direct
EURe transfers, not atomic swaps. See
docs/model_review/gpay_topup_capture_probe.md.

Scope (broadest): all Crypto Deposits into currently-GA-owned wallets, all
tokens. Two narrowing toggles are intentionally NOT applied and can be added
as a one-line WHERE: self-funding exclusion (counterparty = the wallet's GA
owner) and a temporal filter for deposits predating GA ownership of an
imported wallet.

from the GA launch (2025-11-12) on, attributed to the safe's first GA owner
(ga_user) via the int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_wallets bridge. Structural twin
of int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_topups; excludes 'Crypto Deposit' (already the

int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_wallets.description:
Gnosis Pay wallets (Safes) that have been or currently are controlled
by a Gnosis App user, via the Safe's Zodiac **Delay Module**.

Heuristic (Dune query 6675111, reviewed April 2026):

  The Delay Module bound to each GP Safe has its OWN access control —
  Zodiac's enableModule(address)/disableModule(address) functions,
  which emit EnabledModule/DisabledModule events. Any address enabled
  as a module on the Delay can queue transactions on the GP Safe.

  A GP wallet is "on Gnosis App" iff a GA user address has been
  enabled (net +1) as a module on its Delay.

Events scanned (from execution.logs):

  EnabledModule  topic0 = 0xecdf3a3e…f8440 (module addr in DATA field)
  DisabledModule topic0 = 0xaab4fa2b…54276 (module addr in DATA field)

Mapping Delay Module → GP Safe comes from
int_execution_gpay_safe_modules.contract_type = 'DelayModule'.

Incremental: on each run, scans only delay modules that had an
EnabledModule/DisabledModule event in the last 30 days (or since
previous-run watermark), then recomputes the FULL event history for
just those modules. delete+insert on unique_key=pay_wallet keeps
unchanged rows from previous runs. Full-refresh scans everything back
to 2023-06-01.

Onboarding classes:

  onboarded_via_ga : the very first module ever enabled on this Delay
                     is a GA user — user went from zero → Gnosis Pay
                     via Gnosis App.
  imported         : a GA user was added as a module later — user
                     already had Gnosis Pay, then linked their GA Safe.

One row per GP Safe. A Safe with multiple GA modules enabled is still
counted once.
int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_wallets.name: int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_wallets

active_vs_heuristic_ratio.description: Ratio of the canonical GT active-user count to the heuristic user count: round(gt_registered_active / heuristic_users, 4). >1 means the GT active set is larger than what the heuristic captures (sizing the heuristic's under-count vs ground truth); can exceed 1. Gotcha: unguarded division -> NaN/Inf if heuristic_users = 0. Unit: ratio (dimensionless).

gt_active_in_heuristic.description: Number of canonical GT active users that the legacy address heuristic ALSO sees: countIf(is_registered_active AND is_heuristic_active). is_heuristic_active (upstream) = identity present in int_execution_gnosis_app_users_current. Measures the overlap/recall of the heuristic against the GT active set. Unit: user count.
gt_active_in_heuristic.name: gt_active_in_heuristic

gt_active_legacy_only.description: Number of canonical GT active users whose activity is purely LEGACY (Metri) with no current-app footprint: countIf(is_registered_active AND legacy_app_signal AND NOT current_app_signal). Upstream legacy_app_signal = has_swap_metri OR has_metri_fee OR has_metri_transfer OR has_investment OR has_auto_topup; current_app_signal = has_swap_gnosis_io OR is_heuristic_active OR has_cashback OR has_pay_topup. Isolates users the current-app heuristic structurally misses because they only ever used the legacy app. Unit: user count.
gt_active_legacy_only.name: gt_active_legacy_only

gt_active_missed_by_heuristic.description: Number of canonical GT active users the current-app heuristic CANNOT see (blind spot, ~17.5k): countIf(is_registered_active AND NOT is_heuristic_active). These are largely legacy/non-current-app users invisible to the current-app-only heuristic. Complement of gt_active_in_heuristic within gt_registered_active. Unit: user count.
gt_active_missed_by_heuristic.name: gt_active_missed_by_heuristic

gt_avatar_users.description: Total distinct Circles avatar identities in the envio_ga avatar table (stg_envio_ga__avatars = deduped envio_ga.avatar via envio_latest with composite version). This is the active-user CONTAINMENT SPINE for the heuristic (broader membership than the registry). Unit: identity count. Derived as (SELECT count() FROM stg_envio_ga__avatars).
gt_avatar_users.name: gt_avatar_users

gt_registered_active.description: CANONICAL GT active-user count (~26.6k): number of rows in int_execution_gnosis_app_gt_user_activity where is_registered_active is TRUE = a registered identity that performed at least one APP-TAGGED action (gnosis.io or Metri swap, MetriFee, MetriTransfer, pay-topup, cashback, investment, auto-topup config). This is the headline Gnosis App active-user metric. Unit: user count. Derived as countIf(is_registered_active).
gt_registered_active.name: gt_registered_active

gt_registered_active_incl_circles.description: BROADER (sizing-only, NOT headline) active-user count (~40k): rows where is_registered_active_incl_circles is TRUE = registered identity with any app-tagged action OR any GENERIC untagged Circles/social action (PersonalMint, HubTransfer, PrimaryGroupFee, Erc20WrapperTransfer/wrap, InvitationFee, referral earned/sent). Because generic Circles actions can originate from any Circles client (no app tag), this OVER-reaches 'used the Gnosis App'. Unit: user count. Derived as countIf(is_registered_active_incl_circles).
gt_registered_active_incl_circles.name: gt_registered_active_incl_circles

gt_registry_users.description: Total distinct Circles identities in the envio_ga registry (stg_envio_ga__users = deduped envio_ga.gnosis_app_user via envio_latest). ~301k. This is the ecosystem-wide REGISTERED identity universe (one row per address, tombstoned ids removed), NOT a users/active metric. Unit: identity count. Derived as (SELECT count() FROM stg_envio_ga__users).
gt_registry_users.name: gt_registry_users

heuristic_in_avatar.description: Number of heuristic addresses that are also present in the GT avatar spine: countIf(addr IN (SELECT avatar_address FROM stg_envio_ga__avatars)) over the heur set. Numerator of avatar_containment; expected near-total (~99.98%) because the avatar table is the active-user containment spine. Unit: user count.
heuristic_in_avatar.name: heuristic_in_avatar

heuristic_in_registry.description: Number of heuristic addresses that are also present in the GT registry: countIf(addr IN (SELECT address FROM stg_envio_ga__users)) over the heur set. Numerator of registry_containment. Registry addresses are already lowercased upstream so the lower(address) heur side matches. Unit: user count.
heuristic_in_registry.name: heuristic_in_registry

heuristic_only_vs_registry.description: Heuristic addresses NOT found in the GT registry: heuristic_users - heuristic_in_registry. The residual/uncontained tail of the heuristic relative to the registry (heuristic hits with no registered Circles identity). Unit: user count. Non-negative by construction.
heuristic_only_vs_registry.name: heuristic_only_vs_registry

int_execution_gnosis_app_swaps.description:
Gnosis App swaps — one row per CoW order pre-signed by a GA user through
the Cometh ERC-4337 bundler. Matches the Dune semantic: the anchor is
the PreSignature event, NOT the Trade fill. Orders that are pre-signed
but never filled (cancelled, expired, solver mismatch) are still counted
as app activity.

Strict heuristic (all must hold for a row to appear):
  1. GPv2Settlement.PreSignature event with signed=true
  2. PreSignature tx.to  = ERC-4337 EntryPoint v0.7 (0x…7727de22…)
  3. PreSignature tx.from ∈ Cometh bundlers (dynamic int_execution_gnosis_app_bundlers)
  4. PreSignature owner   ∈ GA users
                            (int_execution_gnosis_app_users_current)

Trade enrichment (tokens, amounts, USD, solver) is a LEFT JOIN — NULL
for unfilled orders. `was_filled` surfaces this as a boolean. Partial
fills produce multiple Trade rows for one PreSignature; for the LEFT
JOIN we pick the first fill (argMin on block_timestamp) and aggregate
amounts via sum so one PreSignature = one output row.

Grain: (transaction_hash, log_index) of the PreSignature event. Row
count on this model = count of GA-app signed orders.

int_execution_gnosis_app_token_offers.description:
Gnosis App token-offer registry — one row per `NextOffer` instance emitted
by the Circles v2 ERC20TokenOfferCycle contracts. Each cycle (there are 3
deployed — v1/v2/v3) periodically emits `NextOfferCreated` for a new sale
instance with a fixed CRC price and per-user CRC cap; users then pay CRC
to receive the cycle's `offerToken` (GNO today).

Sources & join:
  1. CycleConfiguration event on the cycle address — carries offerToken,
     admin, offersStart, offerDuration.
  2. NextOfferCreated event on the same cycle address — carries the
     specific offer (nextOffer) address, tokenPriceInCRC, offerLimitInCRC.
  3. Joined on (contract_address = cycle_address) so each offer is
     enriched with its parent cycle's configuration.
  4. NextOfferTokensDeposited aggregated by offer for supply side.

Token metadata (symbol, decimals) comes from tokens_whitelist, keyed on
the lowercase offer_token_address.
int_execution_gnosis_app_token_offers.name: int_execution_gnosis_app_token_offers

int_execution_gnosis_app_user_activity_d.description:
Foundation table for all Gnosis App user-activity analytics — one row
per (date, address, activity_kind). Every downstream cohort, retention,
churn, DAU/WAU/MAU, and activity-by-action mart derives from this table.

activity_kind enum:
  onboard                 — first-ever heuristic hit for this address
                             (from int_execution_gnosis_app_users_current.
                             first_seen_at). Exactly one row per user.
                             Anchors the cohort_month for retention.
  circles_register_human,
  circles_invite_human,
  circles_trust,
  circles_profile_update,
  circles_fee,
  circles_personal_mint,
  safe_invitation_module  — raw heuristic rows from
                             int_execution_gnosis_app_user_events.
  swap_signed             — PreSignature events (all rows in
                             int_execution_gnosis_app_swaps).
  swap_filled             — subset with was_filled = true.
  topup                   — GA→GP TopUps
                             (int_execution_gnosis_app_gpay_topups).

int_execution_gnosis_app_user_events.description:
Long-form heuristic event log for Gnosis App user identification.

Seven rules, all keyed off the same chokepoint: a Cometh ERC-4337
bundler (the dynamic allowlist int_execution_gnosis_app_bundlers, which
supersedes the static seeds/gnosis_app_relayers.csv) sent the outer
transaction to the canonical EntryPoint v0.7. Any account that appears as
a parameter inside such a transaction is, by construction, acting through
Gnosis App for that action.

Rules:
  safe_invitation_module  — Safe created in the same Cometh tx that
                            enabled the Circles InvitationModule
                            (0x00738aca…). The Safe address is the
                            user.
  circles_fee             — CRC fee transfer to the Gnosis App fee
                            receiver (0x97FD8f78…) inside a Cometh tx,
                            matched as either an ERC-1155 Hub transfer
                            (rule_app_fee) or, since June 2026, a gCRC
                            ERC-20 Transfer (rule_app_fee_erc20). The
                            receiver was branded "Metri" pre-rebrand;
                            the address is unchanged.
  circles_register_human  — Hub.RegisterHuman event inside a Cometh
                            tx. decoded_params['avatar'] is the user.
  circles_invite_human    — Same RegisterHuman event; the inviter is
                            the user, canonicalized via
                            int_execution_circles_v2_inviter_canonical
                            (invitation-at-scale proxy remapped to the
                            real origin inviter).
  circles_trust           — Hub.Trust event inside a Cometh tx.
                            decoded_params['truster'] is the user.
  circles_profile_update  — NameRegistry.UpdateMetadataDigest event
                            inside a Cometh tx.
                            decoded_params['avatar'] is the user.
  circles_personal_mint   — Personal CRC mint (Human avatar minting
                            its own Circles, via
                            int_execution_circles_v2_mint_events
                            mint_kind = 'personal') inside a Cometh
                            tx. The mint recipient is the user.

Address columns are stored lowercase WITH the 0x prefix to match the
rest of the dbt outputs and the format that decode_logs produces for
decoded_params address values. Rule 1 reads from int_execution_safes
(which is already 0x-prefixed) and rules 2-6 read from
contracts_circles_v2_*_events.decoded_params (also 0x-prefixed).

Privacy: this is the source-of-truth intermediate for sector
membership. Raw addresses are kept here because they are required
for the snapshot argMax and for the cross-reference with
int_execution_safes. The pseudonymization boundary is in
int_execution_gnosis_app_user_identities, one model downstream.

int_execution_gpay_conversions.description:
GP conversion registry. One row per (conversion event, identity_role)
pair via the bridge fan-out — every chain conversion on a GP Safe
produces one row per pseudonym × role tied to that Safe. Persona
picks the analytical grain at query time:

  WHERE conversion_kind='gpay_payment' AND identity_role='initial_owner'
    → owner grain (one human → one row per payment from any owned Safe)
  WHERE conversion_kind='gpay_payment' AND identity_role='safe_self'
    → treasury grain (one Safe → one row per payment)
  WHERE conversion_kind='gpay_payment' AND identity_role='delegate'
    → operator grain (rarely useful; delegates are usually backend keys)

v1 conversion sources:
  gpay_payment        — int_execution_gpay_activity WHERE action='Payment'
  gpay_cashback_claim — int_execution_gpay_activity WHERE action='Cashback'
  gpay_funded         — first inflow (`Fiat Top Up` or `Crypto Deposit`)
                        into a Safe across the FULL history. Computed
                        via per-Safe `argMin`/`min` over all-time activity
                        (not microbatch-bounded — "first" is global) and
                        then filtered to rows whose first_inflow_ts falls
                        in the target window.

`int_execution_gpay_activity` has no `log_index`, so
`conversion_dedup_key` is built from (transaction_hash, token_address,
counterparty, direction, identity_role) — the activity table's
natural unique tuple plus the role fan-out.

int_execution_gpay_roles_events.description:
Decoded events from the Zodiac Roles v2 module proxies attached to GP
Safes. Includes the events Gnosis Pay actually mutates:

  RolesModSetup    — module enabled and bound to a Safe
  AssignRoles      — spender delegate assignment.
                     roleKeys (bytes32[]) and memberOf (bool[]) are
                     parallel arrays — we ARRAY JOIN them so each row
                     is one (member, role_key, is_member) triple.
  SetDefaultRole   — default role assignment for a delegate
  SetAllowance     — allowance / daily-limit creation or update
  ConsumeAllowance — allowance burn-down on a successful card spend

decode_logs returns decoded_params as a Map(String, String). Array
params are stored as JSON array strings (toJSONString of the decoded
array). ClickHouse JSONExtract* functions are 1-indexed.

ClickHouse alias-shadowing gotcha: SELECT aliases shadow source columns
in WHERE clauses, so writing `SELECT 'X' AS event_name FROM decoded WHERE
event_name = 'X'` evaluates the WHERE against the alias literal (always
TRUE). Combined with UNION ALL + ReplacingMergeTree, this would silently
relabel every row with the last-unioned CTE's literal event_name and drop
AssignRoles entirely. The AssignRoles, SetAllowance and ConsumeAllowance
CTEs all wrap their FROM in a pre-filter subquery (`FROM (SELECT * FROM
decoded WHERE event_name = 'X') d`) so the WHERE runs in a scope where
nothing shadows event_name. The pre-filter subquery is also required for
AssignRoles' ARRAY JOIN — ClickHouse evaluates the range() expression
before the outer WHERE, so without the subquery non-AssignRoles rows
reach the ARRAY JOIN with NULL roleKeys and `range(1, JSONLength(NULL)+1)`
fails with `Illegal (null) value`.

int_execution_gpay_spender_events.description:
Decoded events from the Gnosis Pay Spender module proxies attached to
GP Safes. The Spender is GP's custom final gatekeeper for card-spend
authorization (deployed and controlled by GP's settlement infra).

Events of interest:

  Spend(asset, account, receiver, amount)
      — THE event. Fired on every successful card transaction. The
        headline analytics signal for GP card activity.
            asset    — token being spent (ERC-20 contract address)
            account  — the GP Safe being debited
            receiver — settlement / merchant-acquirer destination
            amount   — token base units (string; could be large)

  AvatarSet(previousAvatar, newAvatar)
      — Spender bound to a Safe (or rebound). The newAvatar is the
        GP Safe this Spender module belongs to. Setup signal.

  TargetSet(previousTarget, newTarget)
      — The Spender's target contract changed.

  EnabledModule / DisabledModule
      — Sub-modules of the Spender enabled or disabled (the Spender
        itself acts as a module manager for its own sub-stack).

  ExecutionFromModuleSuccess / ExecutionFromModuleFailure
      — A sub-module forwarded a call through the Spender.

  OwnershipTransferred / Initialized
      — Standard ownable / proxy lifecycle.

  HashExecuted / HashInvalidated
      — Signed-message tracking. The parameter is an unnamed bytes32
        so we cannot pluck it by key — we just record the event fired
        and leave the bytes32 in the raw decoded_params for downstream
        consumers that need it.

int_execution_gpay_user_events_unified.description:
Long-form GP-side chain event log keyed by
(`user_pseudonym`, `identity_role`). Source:
`int_execution_gpay_activity` joined to the GP identity bridge on
the lowercased Safe address — every chain event on a GP Safe
fan-outs to all (pseudonym, role) pairs tied to that Safe. A
payment from a 2-owner Safe yields 3 rows: `safe_self` + two
`initial_owner`s.

`event_kind` is derived from `int_execution_gpay_activity.action`
via a `multiIf`:
  Payment            → gp.payment
  Cashback           → gp.cashback_claim
  Fiat Top Up        → gp.deposit
  Crypto Deposit     → gp.deposit
  Fiat Off-ramp      → gp.withdrawal
  Crypto Withdrawal  → gp.withdrawal
  Reversal           → gp.payment
  <anything else>    → gp.action_other

v1 is chain-only. Cross-domain Mixpanel touchpoints on a GP Safe's
owner are reached by joining this table to
`int_execution_gnosis_app_user_events_unified` on `user_pseudonym`
— same hash space across sectors.

`event_dedup_key` excludes `log_index` because
`int_execution_gpay_activity` doesn't carry one; the dedup tuple is
(transaction_hash, token_address, counterparty, direction,
identity_role).
